name: Bill Ayers
role: American educator, writer and former Weather Underground organizer
summary: Ayers advocates revolutionary change, democratic education and redistribution according to need. His recent work emphasizes abolition of police and prisons, mass organizing and electoral participation, while he continues defending past political destruction of property.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Supports street movements demanding higher minimum wages.

unions-good.rationale: Praises teachers’ unions for defending learning and workers.

property-fundamental.rationale: Would transfer private educational endowments to democratic public control.

cut-welfare.rationale: Proposes guaranteed income support for unemployed people.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Condemns pervasive surveillance as part of oppressive social control.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Supports drug decriminalization, without specifying a legal retail market.

limit-guns.rationale: Proposes removing street guns, including state agents’ weapons.

empower-police-military.rationale: Redirects policing resources toward community support.

rehabilitation.rationale: Replaces punitive prosecution with rehabilitation and restorative justice.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Welcomes the transformation that made same-sex marriage possible.

abortion-legal.rationale: Condemns Dobbs and attacks on women’s bodily integrity.

gradual-change.rationale: Rejects confinement to incremental changes deemed politically possible.

nation-first.rationale: Rejects American exceptionalism and advocates an equal place among nations.

political-violence-never.rationale: Still defends politically motivated property destruction, while distinguishing it from harming people.

military-superiority.rationale: Rejects the United States acting as an exceptionally dominant warrior nation.

direct-action.rationale: Prioritizes organizing but explicitly insists voting remains vital; advocates both forms of action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Connects liberation with recognizing others’ agency and building humane relationships during organizing.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Explicitly endorses distribution according to need.

school-vouchers.rationale: Rejects vouchers that divert public resources toward private and religious schools.

national-mission.rationale: Rejects claims of American moral superiority over other peoples.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Describes systematic male supremacy and women’s second-class treatment.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Criticizes Democratic opportunism and Republican oligarchic rule.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Proposes extensive public health, housing, education and income provision.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Explicitly affirms equal rights and incalculable value for every human being.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Defends attacks on government property as political opposition.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Condemns book bans and political policing of classroom reading.

death-penalty.rationale: Advocates organizing to abolish executions, citing Illinois as a model.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rejects the Electoral College as an anti-democratic obstacle to meaningful voting.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Now rejects competing militarily with the state and advocates mass movements.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Says capitalism cannot resolve its fundamental crises.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Urges sustained participation in organizing and struggles for justice.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Rejects endless consumption as a false dream that leads to disaster.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Calls capitalism historically progressive against feudalism, while condemning its contemporary exploitation.

socialized-care.rationale: Proposes free childcare for poor students.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Recognizes the destruction of European Jews and criticizes delayed American recognition.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemns suppression of campus protests and restrictions on academic inquiry.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Calls for vibrant public participation and democratic educational communities.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Insists race and class cannot be separated and links multiple liberation struggles.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Describes government by oligarchs and enormous campaign funding as corrupting democracy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Explicitly seeks police and prison abolition through alternative safety institutions.

second-chamber.rationale: Calls the Senate an archaic institution of anti-democracy to be abolished.

free-public-college.rationale: Proposes free quality education through redistribution of university endowments.

public-service-media.rationale: Opposes stripping funding from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Explicitly rejects mandatory minimums and repeat-offender enhancements.

voter-id.rationale: Lists new identification requirements among contemporary voter-suppression measures.

women-suffrage.rationale: Praises suffragists for winning women’s voting rights as an emancipatory transformation.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Identifies enduring structural white supremacy as central to American society.

material-over-identity.rationale: Rejects separating class interests from racial oppression and criticizes an exclusively white working-class framing.

notes: Recent explicit positions take precedence over early underground strategy. Property destruction is distinguished from attacks on people. Drug decriminalization is narrower than full legalization. Refugee protection does not establish a general immigration-level position. Relatives’ views and guests’ remarks are not attributed to Ayers. All remaining null statements reviewed against the gathered evidence; no living-person inferences.
